name: Dichloromethane
typicalUses: Common inert solvent for oxidations, acylations and chromatography
chemoselectivity: Neither acidic, basic, oxidising nor reducing under normal conditions
pitfalls: Not completely inert: reacts with azide (explosive diazidomethane) and slowly with some amines

name: Hexane
typicalUses: Non-polar solvent for extractions and chromatography
chemoselectivity: An alkane: no acidic, basic or redox chemistry under normal conditions
pitfalls: Flammable; n-hexane is neurotoxic (heptane is a safer substitute)

name: Toluene
typicalUses: Solvent for reactions above 100 °C and for Dean–Stark water removal
chemoselectivity: Inert as a solvent under most conditions
pitfalls: Not inert towards strong electrophiles (Friedel–Crafts) or very strong bases (benzylic deprotonation)
